key_insight: A genome-guided framework enables the discovery of stable, lead-free double perovskite absorbers with strong optical properties for various optoelectronic applications.
engineering_relevance: The findings provide actionable design rules for developing sustainable and efficient materials for photovoltaics and sensors.
method: Used 1,221 DFT-calculated compounds to train machine-learning models.
Implemented a staged inverse-design constraint stack on 13,088 compositions.
Identified five phase-stable semiconductor candidates through predictive modeling.
evidence_signal: The machine-learning surrogates achieved a ROC-AUC of 0.92 for stability and an R2 of 0.93 for band-gap prediction.
watch_item: Careful validation is needed to ensure that the identified compositions maintain stability in practical applications.
paper_title: Genome-Guided Interpretable Screening of Phase-Stable, Lead-Free Double Perovskite Absorbers for All-Inorganic Semiconductors, Sensors, and Photovoltaics with DFT-Validated Design Rules
